metadata.title: Jasmine Linguaskill Vocabulary
metadata.notice: Independent vocabulary practice; not an official Cambridge word list.

cards.definitionEn: v. do away with
cards.definitionZh: vt. 廢止, 革除, 消滅

examples.text: Lincoln set out to abolish slavery in the United States.
If God really existed, it would be necessary to abolish him.
An overwhelming majority voted to abolish the brutal punishment.

cards.definitionEn: v. become imbued · v. take up mentally
cards.definitionZh: vt. 吸收, 使全神貫注, 同化, 買進, 理解, 承受, 忍受, 承擔

examples.text: I can't absorb all of the lesson in an hour.
I tried to absorb as much of local culture as possible.
It feels like it's going to absorb you into another world.

cards.definitionEn: n. (chemistry) a process in which one substance permeates another; a fluid permeates or is dissolved by a liquid or solid · n. (physics) the process in which incident radiated energy is retained without reflection or transmission on passing through a medium
cards.definitionZh: n. 吸收, 專心, 全神貫注

examples.text: Let's explain the difference between absorption and adsorption.
What's the difference between absorption and adsorption?
This paper has very good absorption.

cards.definitionEn: v. move faster · v. cause to move faster
cards.definitionZh: v. 加速, 促進

examples.text: Sami's life began to accelerate at an incredible pace.
What should we do to accelerate it?
The policy will only accelerate inflation.

cards.definitionEn: n. the state of being acceptable and accepted · n. (contract law) words signifying consent to the terms of an offer (thereby creating a contract)
cards.definitionZh: n. 接受, 接納, 承認, 同意, 贊同, 容忍, 相信

examples.text: Reading this sentence constitutes acceptance of its Terms and Conditions.
Reading this sentence constitutes acceptance of its terms and conditions.
Is there peace in acceptance?

cards.definitionEn: a. capable of being reached · s. capable of being read with comprehension
cards.definitionZh: a. 易接近的, 可進入的, 可使用的, 易受影響的, 可理解的

examples.text: They focus on making art accessible to all.
Uteral implants for trans women will one day be possible and accessible.
10,000 Days is Tool's most accessible album.

cards.definitionEn: v. provide with something desired or needed · v. have room for; hold without crowding
cards.definitionZh: vt. 使適應, 調和, 通融, 容納, 向...提供；vi. 適應

examples.text: The motel can accommodate as many as 400 guests.
We can accommodate him for the night.
Unfortunately, we're unable to accommodate your request.

cards.definitionEn: n. the action of accomplishing something
cards.definitionZh: n. 成就, 完成

examples.text: Tell me about an accomplishment you are most proud of.
What is your child's proudest accomplishment?
What is your proudest accomplishment?

cards.definitionEn: n. the act of granting rights
cards.definitionZh: n. 一致, 和諧

examples.text: I will sell the boat in accordance with your orders.
We played the game in accordance with the new rules.
We have finished the work in accordance with her instructions.

cards.definitionEn: r. in accordance with
cards.definitionZh: adv. 相應地, 因此, 於是

examples.text: Accordingly as people become rich, they are apt to be stingy.
Living is dear, accordingly we have to economize.
You must assess the situation and act accordingly.

cards.definitionEn: n. responsibility to someone or for some activity
cards.definitionZh: n. 負有責任, 可說明性

examples.text: Spirituality is often just religion with even less accountability.
Police unions exist to shelter police officers from accountability for their actions.
They create a culture of accountability.

cards.definitionEn: s. liable to account for one's actions
cards.definitionZh: a. 負有責任的, 可說明的, 可解釋的

examples.text: I am not accountable to you for my actions.
Every sane man is accountable to his conscience for his behavior.
I am accountable to him for the loss.

cards.definitionEn: n. someone who maintains and audits business accounts
cards.definitionZh: n. 會計人員, 會計師

examples.text: Allan was lucky and passed the tax accountant examination.
The company took action against its former accountant.
The accountant was blamed for the mistake.

cards.definitionEn: n the act of accumulating
cards.definitionZh: n. 自然增長, 自然增長額

examples.text: The report highlights the importance of accrual.
They talked about accrual during the meeting.
Accrual can affect how people make decisions.

cards.definitionEn: v. grow by addition · v. come into the possession of
cards.definitionZh: vi. 自然增加, 產生

examples.text: Many advantages accrue to society from the freedom of speech.
Interest will begin to accrue after the first year.
Benefits accrue to the community from reconstruction.

cards.definitionEn: v. collect or gather
cards.definitionZh: v. 積聚, 堆積

examples.text: We studied the Concordance to Shakespeare to accumulate examples of alliteration.
Car windows accumulate frost on winter mornings.
We accumulate our opinions at an age when our understanding is at its weakest.

cards.definitionEn: n. the act of accumulating · n. (finance) profits that are not paid out as dividends but are added to the capital base of the corporation
cards.definitionZh: n. 積聚, 累積, 積聚物

examples.text: A cloud is an accumulation of water vapour in the sky.
Aluminum accumulation in the bone marrow results in osteomalacia.
Her only interest is the accumulation of money.

cards.definitionEn: n. the quality of being near to the true value · n. (mathematics) the number of significant figures given in a number
cards.definitionZh: n. 精確, 正確

examples.text: The accuracy of his predictions was startling.
Users validate the accuracy of donated clips, checking that the speaker read the sentence correctly.
Donate your voice, validate the accuracy of other people’s clips, make the dataset better for everyone.

cards.definitionEn: r. with few mistakes · r. strictly correctly
cards.definitionZh: adv. 正確地, 精確地

examples.text: Click the play icon. Did they say the sentence accurately?
I don't remember my father's face accurately.
I don't remember my grandmother's face accurately.

cards.definitionEn: n. a formal charge of wrongdoing brought against a person; the act of imputing blame or guilt · n. an assertion that someone is guilty of a fault or offence
cards.definitionZh: n. 控告, 指控, 指責

examples.text: He denies this accusation and speaks only of a kiss.
I can't find any evidence to support your accusation.
He is under a false accusation.

cards.definitionEn: n. any of various water-soluble compounds having a sour taste and capable of turning litmus red and reacting with a base to form a salt · n. street name for lysergic acid diethylamide
cards.definitionZh: n. 酸, 酸類物質, 尖刻, 迷幻藥；a. 酸的, 酸性的, 尖刻的, 敏銳的

examples.text: I choked on some stomach acid and woke up.
I sold Tom two hits of acid.
Citric acid used to give me migraines.

cards.definitionEn: n. a unit of area (4840 square yards) used in English-speaking countries · n. a territory of western Brazil bordering on Bolivia and Peru
cards.definitionZh: n. 英畝

examples.text: Tom bought an acre of land near the lake.
Dan bought an acre of land in Nevada.
Tom works on a 300-acre Christmas tree farm.

cards.definitionEn: r. in an active manner
cards.definitionZh: adv. 活躍地, 積極地

examples.text: Infinite scrolling actively harms users to benefit corporate interests.
In the US capital, restaurants and bars are actively raising funds to help.
Facebook is actively manipulating your mind.

cards.definitionEn: s. advocating or engaged in activism
cards.definitionZh: n. 激進主義分子

examples.text: Helen Keller was a socialist, antimilitarist, and disability rights activist.
Tom is a disability rights activist.
Jamie Reed is a far-right anti-trans activist who has repeatedly been caught in lies.

cards.definitionEn: r. in an adequate manner or to an adequate degree
cards.definitionZh: adv. 足夠地, 適當地

examples.text: Never attribute to malice that which is adequately explained by stupidity.
The various theoretical frameworks have failed to adequately explain this phenomenon.
Without water, healthcare workers won't be able to wash their hands adequately.

cards.definitionEn: v. be compatible or in accordance with · v. follow through or carry out a plan without deviation
cards.definitionZh: vi. 依附, 粘著, 堅持, 追隨, 擁護；vt. 使粘附

examples.text: Players must adhere to the rules of the game.
There will be chaos unless we all adhere to the rules.
Muslims adhere to the teaching of the prophet Mohammed.

cards.definitionEn: v. work in an administrative capacity; supervise or be in charge of · v. perform (a church sacrament) ritually
cards.definitionZh: vt. 管理, 料理, 執行；vi. 執行遺產管理人的職責, 給予幫助

examples.text: The syringe is the instrument most commonly used to administer insulin.
There is a dearth of available medical personnel to administer vaccines.
Ziri entered the cabin and found drugs and things used to administer them.

cards.definitionEn: a. of or relating to or responsible for administration
cards.definitionZh: a. 管理的, 行政的

examples.text: Please forward the document to the administrative office for review.
I made it so only root could access the administrative screen.
Bangladesh is divided into eight administrative divisions.

cards.definitionEn: n. someone who administers a business · n. the party appointed by a probate court to distribute the estate of someone who dies without a will or without naming an executor
cards.definitionZh: n. 管理人, 行政官

examples.text: Not an anna in hand, but call me administrator nonetheless.
Tom is an office administrator at an electronics company.
With Windows OS systems 'administrator account' corresponds to 'root'.

cards.definitionEn: n. the act of admitting someone to enter · n. an acknowledgment of the truth of something
cards.definitionZh: n. 准許進入, 入場費, 錄用, 承認

examples.text: Please tell me the requirements for admission to the college.
His admission that he had stolen the money astonished his family.
Some of them required intubation and admission to the intensive care unit.

cards.definitionEn: n. the act of accepting with approval; favorable reception · n. a legal proceeding that creates a parent-child relation between persons not related by blood; the adopted child is entitled to all privileges belonging to a natural child of the adoptive parents (including the right to inherit)
cards.definitionZh: n. 採用, 採納, 收養

examples.text: I think I'll put up my child for adoption.
The puppy's single good eye begs me for adoption.
Same-sex adoption rights are an important issue for the LGBT* community.

cards.definitionEn: s. contrary to your interests or welfare · s. in an opposing direction
cards.definitionZh: a. 不利的, 敵對的, 相反的, 逆的

examples.text: Our plane was cancelled because of adverse weather conditions.
The rehearsal was cancelled because of adverse weather conditions.
Many intelligent people are not adverse to sex.

cards.definitionEn: n. someone whose business is advertising
cards.definitionZh: n. 做廣告者, 廣告客戶

examples.text: She works as an advertiser at a New Jersey firm.
The advertiser didn't run our ad.
The annoying advertiser called my house.

cards.definitionEn: n an expert who gives advice
cards.definitionZh: n. 顧問, 勸告者, 指導教師

examples.text: I wonder what my old faculty advisor is up to.
Professor Jackson is my faculty advisor.
Tom is my faculty advisor.

cards.definitionEn: n. an announcement that usually advises or warns the public of some threat · s. giving advice
cards.definitionZh: a. 顧問的, 諮詢的, 勸告的

examples.text: The committee can only act in an advisory capacity.
A wind advisory is in effect until the storm front passes.
Tom is a member of the advisory board.

cards.definitionEn: n. a subordinate or subsidiary associate; a person who is affiliated with another or with an organization · n. a subsidiary or subordinate organization that is affiliated with another organization
cards.definitionZh: vt. 使緊密聯絡, 使附屬, 接納, 收養；vi. 發生聯絡, 參加

examples.text: Why did you decide to affiliate yourself with Company A?
When you buy a product using one of my affiliate links, the company pays me.
Check with your local affiliate of our network to find out when the program will be broadcast.

cards.definitionEn: s that you have the financial means for

examples.text: You wouldn't happen to know of an affordable hotel nearby?
Solar power has become much more affordable in recent years.
I just want an affordable place to live.

cards.definitionEn: r happening at a time subsequent to a reference time
cards.definitionZh: adv. 然後, 後來

examples.text: She was very well before lunch, but felt sick afterward.
Only afterward did he explain why he did it.
I didn't remember his name until afterward.

cards.definitionEn: n. material such as sand or gravel used with cement and water to make concrete, mortar, or plaster · n. a sum total of many heterogenous things taken together
cards.definitionZh: n. 合計, 總計, 聚集體；a. 合計的, 聚集的；v. 聚集, 集合, 合計達

examples.text: Heliotrope is a mineral aggregate commonly also known as bloodstone.
Strawberries and raspberries are both examples of an aggregate fruit.
Simply put, a human being is an aggregate of many cells.

cards.definitionEn: n. the class of people engaged in growing food
cards.definitionZh: n. 農業；[機] 農業, 農學

examples.text: Industrialized agriculture is a major contributor to climate change.
The economy of Bangladesh is based on agriculture, manufacturing, and services.
The economy of Bangladesh is mainly based on agriculture and the garment industry.

cards.definitionEn: n. an airfield equipped with control tower and hangars as well as accommodations for passengers and cargo
cards.definitionZh: n. 飛機場；[機] 航空站, 機場

examples.text: I was only at the Boston airport for an hour.
Someone was following me at the airport.
It was bedlam at the airport.

cards.definitionEn: n a flat wing-shaped process or winglike part of an organism · n a wing of an insect
cards.definitionZh: interj. 唉

examples.text: Lone lions, alas, always end up being hunted and haggard.
Alas, that's the kind of world we live in.
Alas! You do not know me, Sir.

cards.definitionEn: conj. Even though; although; notwithstanding.
cards.definitionZh: conj. 儘管, 雖然

examples.text: I wanted to congratulate you, albeit belatedly, on passing your exam.
Have you ever eaten javelina? It's quite good, albeit somewhat gamey.
Tom hopes to make a profit this year, albeit a small one.

cards.definitionEn: n. condition of heightened watchfulness or preparation for action · n. a warning serves to make you more alert to danger
cards.definitionZh: a. 警覺的, 靈敏的, 留心的；n. 警報；vt. 使警覺, 通知, 使意識到

examples.text: I feel more alert after drinking a cup of coffee.
The alert guard perceived a dim shape in the distance.
My watchdog is alert to the slightest sound and movement.

cards.definitionEn: n. a precise rule (or set of rules) specifying how to solve some problem
cards.definitionZh: n. 演算法

examples.text: My algorithm has a 99% success rate.
I wrote the algorithm in Pascal.
Then we can continue the algorithm.

cards.definitionEn: v. place in a line or arrange so as to be parallel or straight · v. be or come into adjustment with
cards.definitionZh: vi. 排列, 排成一行, 結盟；vt. 使結盟, 使成一行, 校正

examples.text: We can use braces to align your teeth better.
Should the stars align, the night will be unforgettable.
Align all the soldiers for their daily checkup.

cards.definitionEn: a. having the same or similar characteristics · r. equally
cards.definitionZh: a. 相似的, 同樣的；adv. 一樣, 以同樣的方式

examples.text: The approaches used in those two designs are exactly alike.
Paul has three sons. They look very much alike.
The Finnish and Faroese flags look too much alike.

cards.definitionEn: n. (law) a formal accusation against somebody (often in a court of law) · n. statements affirming or denying certain matters of fact that you are prepared to prove
cards.definitionZh: n. 斷言, 主張, 申辯

Tom neither confirmed nor denied the allegation.

cards.definitionEn: r. according to what has been alleged
cards.definitionZh: adv. 依其申述

The injaculation method allegedly enables men to have multiple orgasms.
One organization allegedly controls the European drug market.

cards.definitionEn: n. the state of being allied or confederated · n. a connection based on kinship or marriage or common interest
cards.definitionZh: n. 聯盟, 聯合

examples.text: Hitler dreamt of an alliance with the British Empire.
The intergalactic alliance was in danger of collapsing.
They agreed on an alliance.

cards.definitionEn: v. distribute according to a plan or set apart for a special purpose
cards.definitionZh: vt. 分派, 分配

cards.definitionZh: n. 配置, 分配, 撥給

The President shall promulgate a regulation providing for the mandatory allocation of crude oil.
Allocation of resources can be a difficult task when you have no resources at all.

cards.definitionEn: n. an amount allowed or granted (as during a given period) · n. a sum granted as reimbursement for expenses
cards.definitionZh: n. 津貼, 零用錢, 限額, 折扣, 允許；vt. 定量供應

examples.text: You must make allowance for his lack of experience.
My allowance does not pay for my tuition.
We must make allowance for his age.

cards.definitionEn: n. the 1st letter of the Greek alphabet · n. the beginning of a series or sequence
cards.definitionZh: n. 希臘字母表的第一個字母, 最初, 開端

examples.text: My uncle Tom is an alien from Alpha Centauri.
You've been letting Cookie act like the alpha dog.
Cookie thinks he's the alpha dog.

cards.definitionEn: n. a silvery ductile metallic element found primarily in bauxite
cards.definitionZh: n. 鋁

examples.text: There was a time when aluminum was more expensive than gold.
You shouldn't put aluminum foil in the microwave.
Aluminum foil is more expensive than plastic wrap.

cards.definitionEn: n. a diplomat of the highest rank; accredited as representative from one country to another · n. an informal representative
cards.definitionZh: n. 大使

examples.text: The ambassador will be recalled from his present post soon.

cards.definitionEn: n. a cherished desire · n. a strong drive for success
cards.definitionZh: n. 野心, 志向

I have no ambition to outshine him or any other erudite.

cards.definitionEn: a. having a strong desire for success or achievement · s. requiring full use of your abilities or resources
cards.definitionZh: a. 有野心的, 抱負不凡的, 雄心勃勃的

examples.text: The ambitious man became intoxicated with his own success.
His next production was a very ambitious musical.
Man may well, in his attempt to be too ambitious, destroy himself.

cards.definitionEn: v. make amendments to
cards.definitionZh: vt. 修改, 改善, 改良；vi. 改過自新

examples.text: The Diet is likely to amend this unpopular law.

Some people want to amend the constitution.

cards.definitionEn: prep. See Amidst. · prep. In the midst or middle of; surrounded or encompassed by
cards.definitionZh: prep. 在其間, 在其中

She was standing amid the ruins of the castle.
Dozens of injured protesters were taken to hospitals amid the heat and clamor.

cards.definitionEn: prep. Mixed or mingled; surrounded by. · prep. Conjoined, or associated with, or making part of the
cards.definitionZh: prep. 在...當中, 在...之間, 在...之中

I don't like families that quarrel amongst themselves.

cards.definitionEn: n. the reduction of the value of an asset by prorating its cost over a period of years · n. payment of an obligation in a series of installments or transfers

examples.text: The article uses the word amortization in an important context.
Listen for amortization when the speaker explains the situation.
The meaning of amortization becomes clearer from the whole sentence.

cards.definitionEn: v. liquidate gradually
cards.definitionZh: vt. 攤還, 攤銷, 分期償還

examples.text: The team may need to amortize before making a decision.
They agreed to amortize when the situation changed.
A clear plan can help people amortize effectively.

cards.definitionEn: a. using or subjected to a methodology using algebra and calculus · a. using or skilled in using analysis (i.e., separating a whole--intellectual or substantial--into its elemental parts or basic principles)
cards.definitionZh: a. 分析的, 善於分析的, 解析的

examples.text: This is an analytic language.

The manager described the proposal as analytic.

cards.definitionEn: a using or skilled in using analysis (i.e., separating a whole--intellectual or substantial--into its elemental parts or basic principles) · a of a proposition that is necessarily true independent of fact or experience
cards.definitionZh: a. 分析的, 善於分析的, 解析的；[機] 分析的

examples.text: Can we use Scientific calculators on the analytical chemistry test?
René Descartes is the father of analytical thinking.
Heuristics is a search performed through analytical reasoning.

cards.definitionEn: n. the date on which an event occurred in some previous year (or the celebration of it)
cards.definitionZh: n. 週年紀念

On the anniversary of the cataclysm, there was an upsurge in zombie attacks.
Today, December 10, 2023, is the 75th anniversary of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

cards.definitionEn: r. without missing a year
cards.definitionZh: adv. 一年一次, 每年

examples.text: About two million pounds of flour are exported annually.

About two million pounds of wheat were exported annually.

cards.definitionEn: n. income from capital investment paid in a series of regular payments
cards.definitionZh: n. 年金, 年金保險, 年金領受權

examples.text: The law enables us to receive an annuity.
If it weren't for her annuity, she'd never be able to pay the bills.
Poor countess! What a horrible life for her, to be reduced to only thirty thousand pounds of annuity!

cards.definitionEn: n. (Latin) year

examples.text: The article uses the word annum in an important context.
Listen for annum when the speaker explains the situation.
The meaning of annum becomes clearer from the whole sentence.

cards.definitionEn: n. a person who is opposed (to an action or policy or practice etc.) · a. not in favor of (an action or proposal etc.)
cards.definitionZh: n. 反對者, 反對論者；a. 反對的

examples.text: Which anti depressant would you recommend for someone who can not take hormones?
The report highlights the importance of anti.
They talked about anti during the meeting.

cards.definitionEn: s of laws and regulations; designed to protect trade and commerce from unfair business practices
cards.definitionZh: a. 反托拉斯的

examples.text: The purpose of antitrust law is to stop the abusive influence of the market by big companies.

cards.definitionEn: n. a feeling of craving something
cards.definitionZh: n. 食慾, 慾望, 愛好

examples.text: Since being revived, Tom has had a rapacious appetite tor flesh.
My stomach hurts and I’ve lost my appetite.
Tom has a rapacious appetite.

cards.definitionEn: n. fruit with red or yellow or green skin and sweet to tart crisp whitish flesh · n. native Eurasian tree widely cultivated in many varieties for its firm rounded edible fruits
cards.definitionZh: n. 蘋果, 傢伙

examples.text: The apple I gave John is red.
I didn't give Sarah the apple.
We gave Tom the apple.

cards.definitionEn: n. a device or control that is very useful for a particular job · n. durable goods for home or office use
cards.definitionZh: n. 器械, 用具, 應用

cards.definitionEn: s. capable of being applied; having relevance
cards.definitionZh: a. 合適的, 可應用的

cards.definitionEn: n. a person who requests or seeks something such as assistance or employment or admission
cards.definitionZh: n. 申請者

cards.definitionZh: n. 評價, 估價

cards.definitionZh: n. 感激, 賞識, 鑑別

examples.text: I wish to express my deep appreciation for your kindness.

cards.definitionEn: r. in an appropriate manner
cards.definitionZh: adv. 適當的, 恰如其分的, 恰當的, 合適的

cards.definitionEn: v. be close or similar · s. not quite exact or correct

cards.definitionZh: n. 接近, 近似值

Purity is at best an approximation.

cards.definitionZh: n. 套利, 套匯, 仲裁

examples.text: The boardroom grew restive when the CEO discussed complex arbitrage strategies no one fully understood.
The report highlights the importance of arbitrage.
They talked about arbitrage during the meeting.
